name: Residential, House, One Family with Minor Second Unit

rules.title: A home plus a small second unit
rules.plain: RH-1(S) lots are for single-family homes with a minor second unit: two units per lot if the second is 600 sq ft or less (or one per 3,000 sq ft of lot area, up to three), with up to four units (six on a corner lot) under the density exception, plus accessory units.

rules.title: Where height is measured from
rules.plain: Height is measured from the curb at the middle of the building's street front. On a lot that slopes up from the street, only the first 10 feet back are measured from the curb, and the rest from the average ground at the two sides of each cross-section; on a lot that slopes down, the curb is used for the first 100 feet.

rules.title: Height limit
rules.plain: No part of a building may be taller than the height limit mapped for this lot's height and bulk district.

rules.title: RH-1(S) dwelling cap
rules.plain: In RH-1(S), no part of a home may be taller than 35 feet, even where the mapped limit is higher: 40 feet where the rear of the lot is 20 feet or more higher than the front, 30 feet where it is 20 feet or more lower, and 25 feet where it is 40 feet or more lower.

rules.title: Rear yard
rules.plain: The back 30% of the lot, and never less than 15 feet, must stay open at ground level and on every floor.

rules.title: Front setback
rules.plain: The building must step back from the front lot line as far as the neighboring building with the shallower setback, up to 10 feet (15 feet on some block faces, not shown).

rules.title: Front height plane
rules.plain: Above 30 feet, the front of the building must slope back at 45 degrees from the front setback line. It doesn't apply where the rear of the lot is 20 feet or more higher than the front, and next to taller neighbors the plane can start higher; that isn't shown.

rules.title: Narrow streets
rules.plain: On a street 40 feet wide or narrower, upper stories may have to step back from the front; street widths aren't in this app's data, so that isn't shown.

rules.title: Cross-slope
rules.plain: Where the street or the ground slopes across the lot by more than 5%, a wide building is measured from several points, each covering a limited width (65 feet or less, narrower on steeper slopes); this view measures from one point.
